proves: The legacy driver 8-byte-key transform sub_13160/sub_13450 is the same cipher family as the A6B0/A7F0 transform documented from EdpEDiskCtrl.dll: key table EDPSECDISK200709, AES-128 structure, per-block counter tweak.
The transform is offset-tweaked rather than CBC-chained, so correct LBA7 legacy compatibility extent decryption requires the counter seed of the real mount I/O, not an IV.
Six additional key candidates fail to expose structure in the no-password SanDisk LBA7 legacy compatibility extent under the exact driver semantics.
The four physical LBA7 legacy compatibility extent captures share no block-level or positional byte structure, ruling out a cross-disk shared key with shared plaintext template.
The EDPSECDISK marker provides a cheap cross-binary search key and surfaces the Linux client as an unscreened code path.
does_not_prove: That LBA7 legacy compatibility extent was produced or consumed by this cipher family; the true crypto boundary remains unclosed.
That the LBA7 legacy compatibility extent plaintext is structured; a keybag-style inherently high-entropy plaintext is not excluded by any current negative.
Any producer or consumer of LBA7 legacy compatibility extent in the Linux client; the marker hits are a search surface, not address evidence.
